title: Plan a pipeline that makes 50 localised ad versions inside a fixed budget
scenario: A studio plans how to make 50 localised versions of one approved tea ad inside a fixed budget. You review the plan before the first request. Use the exhibit. The brief, the draft, the cards and the numbers are made up for this case. The vendor lines are copied from the docs.
exhibit:
BRIEF:
  Kettle & Leaf tea. One approved master ad with the tagline "Steep slowly.".
  50 versions: 10 markets x 5 sizes. Due Thursday 12:00. Now: Wednesday 08:00.
  Budget cap: $20.

PIPELINE (draft, made up for this case):
  1 Approve master and brand rules   person, once
  2 Localise the tagline             each market, 10 runs
  3 Check each tagline               each market
  4 Make the images                  each version, one batch of 50,
                                     sent Wednesday 20:00
  5 Check each image                 each version
  6 Collect files, sign off, send    all, person

ROLE CARDS (draft, made up for this case):
  Producer      plans, hands out items, collects.      Tools: status sheet
  Localiser     writes one tagline for one market.     Tools: none
  Visual maker  makes one image from the approved
                line and the layout.                   Tools: image tool
  Checker       reads each image against the rubric
                and reports.                           Tools: read files,
                                                       upload to the client folder

STATUS SHEET (draft, made up for this case):
  One row per version. The row key is the row number, 1 to 50.
  The batch requests use ids such as tea-de-9x16.

BUDGET (made up for this case):
  Localise         10 markets x $0.10              = $1.00
  Check taglines   10 markets x $0.10              = $1.00
  Images (batch)   50 images x 2 tries x $0.05     = $5.00
  Check images     100 images x $0.03              = $3.00
  Producer agent   1 run x $5.00                   = $5.00
  Reserve: 20% of the sum of the five lines above.
  Cap: $20.

VENDOR LINES (copied from the docs):
  OpenAI, Batch API: "Each batch completes within 24 hours (and often more
  quickly)."
  Claude, batch processing: "Dry run a single request shape with the
  Messages API to avoid validation errors."
  Gemini, Batch API: "The user-defined key is used in the response to
  indicate which output is the result of which request."
  Claude, subagents: "subagents can be limited to specific tools, reducing
  the risk of unintended actions."

questions.prompt: Step 6 is marked "all". When may it start?

options.text: As soon as the first 25 images pass, so that the client can see progress early
options.explanation: An "all" step waits for every item. Starting early would send an unfinished set.

options.text: Right after step 1, because the master is approved and the other steps can follow it
options.explanation: The master is approved, but the 50 versions do not exist yet. Step 6 needs the finished files.

options.text: After all 50 versions are made, and every single one of them has passed its check
options.explanation: Right. An "all" step runs after every item has finished. This is our once, each, all method from chapter 1.

options.text: As soon as the batch is sent, because the files will exist by the time a person looks
options.explanation: The batch may take up to 24 hours. A person would find missing files.

questions.prompt: Which change fits the role cards?

options.text: Remove the upload tool from the Checker, since it only needs to read the files
options.explanation: Right. Claude lists tool limits as a way to reduce the risk of unintended actions. A checker that reports should not be able to upload.

options.text: Give the Localiser the image tool, so that it can see how each line fits a picture
options.explanation: Making the image is the Visual maker's job. The extra tool adds risk and no value.

options.text: Give the Producer every tool, so that it can fix the work of any role itself
options.explanation: This breaks the point of narrow roles. A producer that plans should not hold every tool.

options.text: Give the Visual maker the upload tool, so that files reach the client a bit sooner
options.explanation: This skips the check and the person's sign-off. Files should not reach the client before both.

questions.prompt: The draft sends all 50 requests as one batch on Wednesday 20:00. What do you change?

options.text: Keep the plan, because batches are often quick and so the Thursday deadline is safe
options.explanation: OpenAI says "often more quickly", but the window is 24 hours. An evening start can pass Thursday 12:00.

options.text: Send the batch on Thursday 08:00, so that the images are as fresh as possible
options.explanation: A batch can take up to 24 hours. A Thursday morning start misses the 12:00 deadline.

options.text: Split the 50 into ten batches of five, so that each small batch is sure to finish in an hour
options.explanation: Each smaller batch still has a 24-hour window. Splitting does not make the deadline safe, and it skips the test run.

options.text: After the taglines pass, test three versions normally, then batch the other 47 that morning
options.explanation: Right. A dry run catches errors early, and a batch can take up to 24 hours. Starting on Wednesday morning leaves time before Thursday 12:00.

questions.prompt: What should the status sheet use as its row key?

options.text: The row number, because results come back in the same order as the requests
options.explanation: Results can come back in any order. The row number would mix up the rows.

options.text: The same id as the batch request, such as tea-de-9x16, in each sheet row
options.explanation: Right. Gemini says the user-defined key shows which output belongs to which request. One id in the batch and the sheet links them.

options.text: The time each result arrived, because no two results arrive at the same moment
options.explanation: Arrival time says nothing about which item a result is. It can also repeat.

options.text: The file size of each image, because every picture has its own size
options.explanation: Sizes can match, and they do not name the item.

questions.prompt: What is the plan total with the reserve?

options.text: About $15.
options.explanation: This is the sum of the five lines, before the reserve is added.

options.text: About $16.20.
options.explanation: This counts only 50 image checks, not 100. The plan checks every try.

options.text: About $18.
options.explanation: Right. 1 + 1 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 15. The reserve is 20% of 15, which is 3. The total is 18, under the $20 cap.

options.text: About $20.
options.explanation: This is the cap, not the plan total.
